chunks.arabic_text: ٢ - الْمُنْفَضِلُ بْنُ عُمَرَ، الْجَعْفِيُّ، أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ. ضَعِيفٌ، مُتَهَافِتٌ، مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ، خَطَّابِيٌّ. وَقَدْ زِيدَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ كَثِيرٌ، وَحَمِلَ الْغُلَاةُ فِي حَدِيثِهِ حَمْلًا عَظِيمًا. وَلَا يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُكْتَبَ حَدِيثُهُ. وَرَوَى عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، وَأَبِي الْحَسَنِ (عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: 2 – Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, al-Juʿfī, Abū ʿAbdillāh. Weak, collapsed, a proponent of irtifāʿ in doctrine, a Khaṭṭābī. Many things have been added (i.e. attributed) upon him, and his ḥadīth carry a great amount of weight with the ghulāt. It is not permissible to write his ḥadīth. He narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) and Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him).

en.summary: Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar al-Juʿfī, a companion of Imam al-Riḍā and Imam al-Jawād, is critiqued by al-Ghadāʾirī for his weakness and tendency toward exaggeration (irtifāʿ), which led the Ghulāt to attribute significant theological innovations to him. The ruling of 'impermissibility to write' (lā yujāzu an yuktaba ḥadīthu) reflects a specific Shia scholarly nuance where his narrations are preserved but not treated as definitive proof in legal derivation due to these doctrinal distortions. This entry highlights the critical process of distinguishing between the Sahaba's reliability and the later sectarian appropriation of their reports.
en.seo_question: Who is Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Umar and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.مُتَهَافِتٌ: Collapsed (prone to errors and mixing up narrations)
key_terms.مُرْتَفِعُ الْقَوْلِ: Proponent of Irtifāʿ (a specific theological doctrine regarding the Imams)
key_terms.الْغُلَاةُ: The Ghulat (Exaggerators, a group known for attributing divine qualities to Imams)
